contract_grounding.note: Per violates-self-check: the assertion is conditional (IF invalid vectors config THEN 400). The observed value {} is not established as inside the constraint's 'invalid' domain: the doc types vectors as 'object or map from strings to objects, Optional' (a degenerate empty map is not explicitly excluded), and the source (see source_grounding) treats Multi(empty) as the designed default state, identical to omitting the field (which also returns 200). Shapes that genuinely match NO variant (null / scalar / array) are rejected 400 exactly as the constraint states (boundary_01 lines 3-21). Hence on the strict reading the constraint is not violated by {}. The competing reading — that the doc's two example modes imply size+distance presence so {} is 'malformed' — has no explicit doc or contract text forbidding the empty shape (checked: no constraint in structured_contract.json declares vectors must be non-empty). Recorded as false with this rationale; final call belongs to chain-auditor.

source_grounding.note: Every grep hit for the claim's keywords (vectors / VectorsConfig / empty-vector error strings) was read; no code path rejects an empty dense-vectors config in v1.18.0. The acceptance of {} is the designed serde/default path (Default and empty() constructors exist precisely for the zero-dense-vectors state used by sparse-only/payload-only collections), while the 'at least one of dense/sparse required' validation exists only as an unimplemented TODO in conversions.rs:94 — i.e., acceptance is by design, and the stricter validation the claim implicitly assumes is acknowledged as missing by the developers themselves. Both facts recorded; auditor weighs them.
